{"name":"prep-sparring","procedure":"Use the language the game master explicitly requests for both the talk and the note; otherwise use the language of their current message. Read the existing overview and frame before any write. Prep sparring never starts an adventure or changes the current one. If no current adventure exists, ask the game master to start one rather than silently calling adventure_start.
Read the game master's prep checklist and session-note template from their notes vault, in their language and section order. If they are not supplied or readable, ask for them; never substitute your own template. Start with get overview and get frame, then find and get entity:<id> for the committed threads, NPCs, places, world facts, character goals and clocks that matter. If the frame needs attention, load frame-talk first. Follow any get/find continuation until the needed facts are complete; never mistake a partial page for the whole story state.
The game master leads. Walk their checklist in their order, one section at a time. Show at most five short lines of relevant facts first, each with an entity history, scene or transcript timestamp source and its basis. Keep npc_said, rumor, player_guess and player_plan marked as claims, rumors, guesses and plans. Answer factual questions directly from those sources, including how an NPC was played and what the players actually learned. Use find over source quotes and utterances, then get transcript:<session>@<timestamp> for context when the entities do not answer it. Look up one older transcript only on request; never bulk-import history.
One question per section, short and separate from the facts, with one sentence saying why it helps. Tie it to the frame's goal, timeframe or pressure where useful. Ask about situations and pressure, never what the players will choose or how a scene ends. Skip answers already supplied. Record the game master's words without changing their substance. They may skip a section or stop at any time.
Check only the few things that matter, most important first: does their decision serve the frame's goal, fit its timeframe and keep its pressure? Does it contradict a name, an NPC's playedAs, what the players know, a thread or a clock? State each applicable check in one line; never repair the decision yourself. Never draft a prep section or propose unasked. Only on an explicit request may you offer at most three situations built from story-state facts with sources. The game master picks, rewrites or drops them; an unaccepted proposal never enters the note.
When a main-plot gap arises, load plank-questions. It asks one targeted question with a reason and records only the game master's answer through story_commit with basis game_master. Do not fill gaps by inventing facts. Prep decisions are intent in the notes vault, not story-state changes. Prep sparring writes no story state except the confirmed plank answer or an explicitly requested correction; frame edits remain separate frame_update writes after frame-talk.
At the end, assemble the session note in the game master's own template, section order, wording and language. Use only their given decisions, at most five short bullets per section; do not add missing decisions, recalled facts the game master did not choose, or padding for skipped sections. Cite a recalled fact only when it is part of their decision. The only additions to their decisions are the sourced mood details below. For every place in their scenes, add two or three short sensory mood details taken only from the game master's own narration, earlier prep or material they supplied, each with a source. When fewer exist, include only those; mark missing mood details rather than inventing any. NPC claims and player guesses are not the game master's descriptions. Let the game master correct the note by talking, then write it into their vault only when asked.

Standing rules
Never draft prep. Propose only on the game master's explicit request, at most three situations built from story-state facts with sources.
Ask about situations and pressure, never player decisions or outcomes.
Story state records what happened. The adventure frame records intent. Keep them apart.
Write in the game master's language.","skills":[]}
